1.why: Reset tokens are bound only to the anonymous browser session that requested them; the account string is discarded and never checked for ownership.

2.why: The reset digest lives in one session record, so the same code cannot verify against a different user's/session's reset state.

3.why: Password update only sets flags on the current session and never invalidates or removes other sessions in the map.

4.why: Server refuses to serve the app without TLS certs and sets HSTS, but the TLS protocol version is not explicitly pinned to the latest.

5.why: Reset tokens are SHA-256 digested and passwords bcrypt-hashed in memory; nothing is encrypted at rest with a reversible cipher, and little user data is stored.

6.why: There is no real email path; the API returns the raw testToken in JSON and the UI displays it, so private reset material is not guarded in transit messages.

7.why: Inputs are type/length-checked and passwords policy-validated; client rendering uses textContent/createTextNode, and user input is not embedded into HTML on the server.

8.why: The only generated link is same-origin pathname plus a hash fragment; no open redirect or external URL parameter is accepted.

9.why: No email templates incorporate user-controlled HTML/scripts; delivery is simulated without composing markup from input.

10.why: Recovery and MFA codes are written to the on-page Logs panel, console, and test-token UI, so tokens are shown in logs.

11.why: Passwords are bcrypt-hashed in session state, but the MFA secret is the hardcoded string "246810" in source and reset digests sit in a process memory map.

12.why: There are no default username/password logins, yet the fixed demo MFA code acts as a known shared credential for every recovery.

13.why: Recovery, password, and MFA paths increment attempt counters with windows/lockouts (429) after several failures.

14.why: Recovery always returns the same generic eligible-account message and does not indicate whether the account exists.

15.why: Reset tokens are 32-byte cryptographically random hex and single-session, but they are not tied to a persisted user identity.
